name: Teen Patti
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Standard rules. Players choose to play blind or seen
Bet in turn. When only two players remain, either can call a show
winner: Best standard hand. Trail > Pure sequence > Sequence > Colour > Pair > High card
notes: The baseline. Good default when nobody wants a twist.

name: AK47
joker: Every Ace, King, 4 and 7 is a joker
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Plays exactly like normal Teen Patti
Any A, K, 4 or 7 in your hand counts as whatever card helps you most
winner: Best standard hand
notes: 16 jokers in the deck. Trails and pure sequences are common, hand values run high.

name: Char Sau Bees
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Card values: Ace = 1, numbers at face value, J/Q/K = 0
Arrange your 3 cards in any order to form a 3 digit number
winner: Closest to 420 wins, over or under
notes: Sister game to 999 but less obvious, since going past 420 is possible. More thinking, more arguing.

name: Chhota Joker
joker: Each player's own lowest card is their personal joker
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Look at your hand and find your lowest ranked card
That card, and any other card of the same rank in your hand, becomes a joker for you only
Every player has a different joker
winner: Best standard hand
notes: If your lowest card is part of a pair, both become jokers, which usually means a trail.

name: Khula Joker
joker: Whatever rank the face-up card is
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
Flip one card from the deck face up in the middle
play: All four cards of that rank become jokers for everyone
Normal play from there
winner: Best standard hand
notes: The shared joker means everyone is on the same footing, unlike Chhota Joker.

name: Padosi
joker: The flipped rank plus the rank directly above and below it
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
Flip one card face up
play: If a 7 is flipped, all 6s, 7s and 8s are jokers. 12 jokers total
Ace wraps around, so an Ace flip makes K, A and 2 wild
winner: Best standard hand
notes: The near-misses are the fun part. People realise their card was one rank off.

name: Muflis
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Normal play, but the entire ranking is flipped
High card beats pair, pair beats sequence, and a trail is the worst hand possible
Within the same category, lower cards win (2-3-5 beats 4-6-9)
Ace counts as the highest card, so it hurts you
winner: Worst standard hand wins
notes: Messes with instincts hard. Agree upfront whether A-2-3 counts as a sequence.

name: Gol Chakkar
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
Dealer calls a pass direction, left or right, before anyone passes
play: Everyone looks at their 3 cards and picks 1 to pass in the called direction
All passes happen at the same time, so you pass before seeing what's coming to you
At the same moment, you receive 1 card from the player on your other side (if everyone passes left, you receive from the player on your right)
Your hand stays at 3 cards, no discard needed
Nobody touches the deck after the deal
winner: Best standard hand
notes: No blind here, you have to look at your hand to know what to pass, so everyone plays seen. With 6 players, what you send is genuinely gone until it comes all the way back around.

name: Tukka
joker: Each player's own called rank, personal to them
setup: Before any cards are dealt, every player calls out a rank out loud so it is locked
Deal 3 cards to each player
play: Your called rank is your personal joker for the round
Everyone has a different one and everyone knows everyone else's
winner: Best standard hand
notes: You commit blind, so it is genuinely 50-50 whether it helps. Table reads get loud.

name: Badalta Joker
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
Flip one card face up. That rank is wild
play: After each betting round, flip a new card
The new rank replaces the old one entirely. The previous joker goes dead
Cap it at three flips total
winner: Best standard hand using whatever the final joker is
notes: Your hand goes from garbage to trail to garbage across three flips. Keep the cap or the round drags.

name: Laal Kaali
joker: Every card of the flipped card's colour
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
Flip one card face up
play: If the flip is red, all 26 red cards are jokers
If black, all 26 black cards. Half the deck goes wild
winner: Best standard hand
notes: Almost everyone lands a trail. Peak chaos. The natural-beats-joker tiebreak matters most here.

name: Beat the B*tch
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to the middle as the side hand. Nobody looks at it
Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Play a full classic Teen Patti round among the players
Once one player has won the round, reveal the side hand
The round winner must beat the side hand with their own hand
winner: The round winner takes the pot only if their hand beats the side hand. If the side hand wins or ties, nobody takes the pot and it rolls over into the next round
notes: Pot can roll over several rounds and get big. Decide upfront whether a tie counts as a loss (recommended: yes).

name: Bhoot Wale Patte
setup: Dealer secretly sets aside 2 cards face down before dealing, unseen by anyone including the dealer
Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Play a fully normal round, betting and folding as usual, down to the final two players
At the show, reveal both secret cards. Those 2 ranks are cursed for this hand
Either finalist holding a cursed rank is disqualified instantly, regardless of hand strength
winner: The clean finalist wins automatically if the other is cursed. If both are clean, best standard hand wins. If both are cursed, the pot rolls into the next hand
notes: A trail of Aces can still lose if Aces turn out to be cursed. The best hand in the room can lose without a single comparison.

name: Kismat Ka Jugad
setup: Boot for this hand is double the usual amount
Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: First betting round plays as normal
To exchange 1 card from your hand for a fresh one from the deck, you must first double the current chaal
Discard the unwanted card face down and draw a replacement
Capped at 2 swaps total per player for the whole hand
Normal betting continues between swaps
winner: Best standard hand
notes: Paying double to sit in, then double again to fix your hand, is either smart play or a trap. Usually a trap.

name: Ek Aankh Khuli
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
The first card dealt to each player is placed face up in front of them, the other 2 stay face down
play: All 6 players have exactly 1 of their 3 cards exposed for everyone to see at all times
Betting and showdown play out normally from there
winner: Best standard hand
notes: The only variation where you're reading the table instead of just your own hand. With 6 exposed cards out, a sharp player can rule out a lot before the first bet lands.

name: Boli Wale Joker
joker: One rank called by the winning bidder, wild for everyone, plus a second personal joker only the bidder holds
setup: Before dealing, the dealer opens an out-loud auction starting at the usual boot
Players call out higher amounts until nobody raises further, the winning bidder pays that amount into the pot
The winning bidder calls a rank out loud before seeing any cards. That rank is wild for the whole table
Deal 3 cards to each player
play: The winning bidder looks at their own hand and secretly picks 1 of their own 3 cards as a personal joker known only to them
Play a normal round otherwise, all disputes go to a full show
winner: Best standard hand. The bidder reveals their secret joker only if they reach the final show
notes: If nobody raises past the opening amount, whoever opened the bidding takes it at that price. The public joker is a blind gamble, the private one is a guaranteed edge, which is why the auction gets loud.

name: Fast Fatka
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Normal play, but every betting decision has a hard count, someone counts to 5 out loud once it's your turn
No chaal, raise, or fold called by the count means you're automatically folded
winner: Best standard hand
notes: One slow player kills the pace for a 6-player table. Use it occasionally, not every hand, or people burn out.

name: Nikal Fenk
setup: Deal 4 cards face down to each player
Everyone looks at their 4 cards and discards 1 face down
play: The remaining 3 cards are your hand
Normal Teen Patti play from there
winner: Best standard hand
notes: Blind play is awkward here since you must look to discard. Usually everyone plays seen.

name: Jodi Bijodi
setup: Before dealing, the dealer declares 'odd' or 'even' for the round
Deal 3 cards to each player
play: If odd is declared, only odd cards (A, 3, 5, 7, 9, J, K) count toward your hand
If even, only even cards (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, Q) count
winner: Best hand made from your qualifying cards. Zero qualifying cards means you are out for the round
notes: Agree upfront where Ace sits. Most groups call it odd.

name: Do Raja
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Normal Teen Patti play, but there are two winners at the end
winner: The best hand and the worst hand both win. Muflis ranking decides the worst
notes: Keeps people in longer since a garbage hand is still live. Works well with a large table.

name: Jodi Joker
joker: Conditional, based on your own hand shape
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: If your hand contains a natural pair, your third card automatically becomes a joker
If you have no pair, you get no joker at all
winner: Best standard hand
notes: Every pair silently upgrades to a trail. Half the table thinks they are unbeatable, then four trails hit the show at once.

name: Sabka Hissa
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
Flip 1 card face up in the middle before betting starts
play: The flipped card belongs to every player at the table
At showdown, each player plays their best 3 out of their own 3 cards plus the shared card
winner: Best standard hand using your best 3 of 4 cards
notes: The one variation where the dealer's flip helps the whole table instead of picking a winner or a victim.

setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Card values: Ace = 1, numbered cards = face value, J/Q/K = 0
Your 3 cards form a 3 digit number and you can arrange them in any order
Aim to get as close to 999 as possible
winner: The player whose number is closest to 999 wins
notes: Some groups play 'closest to 999 or 111' so a terrible hand can also win. Decide before dealing.

name: Murda Patta
setup: Deal 3 cards to each player
Flip 1 card face up before betting starts
play: That rank goes dead instead of wild, all four cards of that rank contribute nothing
A dead card can't be used to form a pair, sequence, or trail, it's just a blank slot
Normal betting and showdown from there using whatever is still live in your hand
winner: Best standard hand using only your live cards
notes: The mirror image of Khula Joker. Instead of hoping you hold the flipped rank, you're praying you don't, since a pair of Kings turns into nothing if Kings just got declared dead.

name: Parda Faash
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
Play a fully normal round down to the final two players
play: Both finalists flip 1 of their 3 cards face up at the same time, then a betting round happens
Both flip a 2nd card, another betting round
The 3rd and final card is flipped together for the actual result
winner: Best standard hand
notes: Every other variation changes the hand itself. This one leaves the cards alone and stretches out the ending instead, so the finalists bet on a slowly unfolding picture instead of one blind flip.

name: Haath Ka Kachra
joker: Three ranks, drawn from the deck after the draft cascade. All four cards of each rank are wild for everyone.
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
Deal the dealer 3 additional cards face down
play: The dealer looks at all 6 cards (their 3 plus the extra 3), keeps their best 3, and passes the other 3 face down to the next player
That player adds the received 3 to their own 3, looks at all 6, keeps their best 3, and passes their unwanted 3 onward
This repeats around the table in turn order until the last player has drafted
The last player's unwanted 3 cards go back into the deck instead of passing on
Shuffle the deck, then draw 3 cards. All four cards of each of those 3 ranks are wild for the whole table
Everyone plays seen from the start, since drafting forces a look. Normal betting proceeds once jokers are revealed
winner: Best standard hand using the 3 joker ranks as wild
notes: Up to 12 cards can be wild at once, so hands run big. What you reject early can end up deciding everyone's hand once it hits the joker draw.

name: Ek Se Badhkar Ek
setup: Deal 5 cards face down to each player
play: Round 1: every player flips their first card face up at the same time, each paying 1 counter into the pot

From round 2 onward, every player still holding cards decides at the same time: flip your next card (pay 1 more counter, chasing the lead) or hold (stop revealing for the rest of the hand, your current best card stays locked in and still counts at the end)
Repeat for up to 5 rounds, or until everyone has either run out of cards or chosen to hold
Whoever holds the single highest card among everyone's revealed cards wins the pot
winner: Highest single card revealed, among players who stayed in. Exact ties (same rank) split the pot evenly
notes: Simulated at 6 players: every seat wins almost exactly 1 in 6 times, genuinely seat-blind, since everyone reveals together instead of taking turns against a moving target. Average pot lands around 13 counters. About 1 in 7 rounds ends in a tie for the top card. The real decision each round is whether to keep paying to chase the lead or lock in what you've got, that's where the skill lives now, not turn order luck.

name: Bidai Wale Joker
joker: The middle card's rank to start, then the open card of whoever packed most recently
setup: Flip 1 card face up in the middle. That rank is the opening joker for everyone
Deal 3 cards to each player, 2 face down and 1 face up in front of them
play: Every player's open card stays visible all round, so the table can see exactly which jokers are waiting to come
The moment a player packs, their open card's rank becomes the new joker and the previous one goes dead
Every pack replaces the joker again, so whatever the last packer showed is what stands at the show
Your own 3 cards are your hand. The middle card only sets the opening joker, it is never part of anyone's hand
winner: Best standard hand using whatever the live joker is at the show
notes: Packing stops being a quiet exit, you hand the table a joker on the way out. Since every open card is visible, folding early means giving away the joker everyone could already see you were sitting on.

name: Antim Faisla
setup: Place 1 card face down in the middle before dealing. Nobody looks at it
Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Play a fully normal round, betting and folding as usual
Nobody knows which direction the hand will be scored while the money is going in
At the show, flip the middle card
winner: Red card means normal ranking and the best hand wins. Black card means Muflis, and the worst hand wins instead
notes: The only twist where you bet a hand you cannot classify yet. A trail is either the best hand at the table or the worst one, and you find out after the last rupee is in.

name: Shun Chekdi
joker: Five ranks per player, either the X or the + of the grid, chosen privately
setup: Lay 9 cards face up in a 3x3 grid in the middle
Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Each player picks one shape from the grid: the X (four corners plus the centre) or the + (middle row plus middle column)
All 5 ranks in your chosen shape are wild for you only
You never announce your choice and you can settle on it whenever you like, before or after looking at your hand
The centre card belongs to both shapes, so that rank is wild for everyone no matter what
winner: Best standard hand using your chosen shape as jokers
notes: Simulated at 6 players picking their better shape: about 37% of hands land a trail, but 1 in 6 still gets no joker at all from either shape. The grid is public and the choice is private, so the reading happens on the table, not in your hand.

name: Upar Neeche
joker: Your own highest and lowest cards, personal to you
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: Your highest ranked card and your lowest ranked card are both wild for you
Any other card sharing a rank with either of them is wild too
With three different ranks that leaves exactly one natural card, your middle one, so every hand reads as a trail of that middle card
A natural pair or trail means all three cards are wild, which reads as a trail of Aces
winner: Best standard hand. In practice the highest middle card takes it, and any natural pair or better beats every unpaired hand
notes: The mirror twin of Chhota Joker taken to its limit. Nobody ever holds a bad hand, so the whole round turns on one card nobody can see until the show. Fastest twist in the set.

name: 1942 A Love Story
joker: Every A, 9, 4 and 2, plus every heart
setup: Deal 3 cards face down to each player
play: The digits of 1942 with Ace as the 1: every Ace, 9, 4 and 2 is wild
Every heart is wild as well, whatever its rank
25 of the 52 cards end up wild, so most hands land a trail
winner: Best standard hand
notes: AK47's fixed ranks crossed with an entire wild suit. Nearly half the deck goes wild, so the natural-beats-joker tiebreak decides more rounds than the hand category does.
